items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: And then later I heard, I got to be a big Dizzy Gillespie fan.

ctx.x: You stated in a recent liner note that Gil Evans’ gig was the greatest one you’ve done. Does that still hold up?

Sure it does. He was, I mean him and Dizzy were the two, to me, two absolute geniuses. And I was lucky enough to work with Gil for a long period of time, and I was lucky enough to experience what he was like as a band leader, which was basically never telling you what to play, maybe giving you a little hint maybe once a year. But basically never telling you what or how to play and just using you, or having you in his musical organization, as long as you played the way he liked. In other words he picked his…
Wow. That’s saying a lot. You said that you started on the trumpet because it was shiny?
